content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by lead-ledger-c5 while re-deriving gr-bl-brief-drift-backfill-714. Two implementations of the SAME normalisation disagree, and the reason they have gone unnoticed is that they look equivalent.

  Go      internal/cli/tasks_create_cmd.go:744
          strings.NewReplacer("**", "", "__", "", "`", "").Replace(description)
          ONE non-overlapping left-to-right pass considering all three patterns at once.

  Elixir  api/lib/barkpark/tasks/brief_mirror.ex:161
          defp strip_markdown(text), do: Enum.reduce(@stripped, text, &String.replace(&2, &1, ""))
          THREE passes, one pattern each, each over the previous pass's result.

WHY THEY LOOK EQUIVALENT AND ARE NOT. The three patterns use DISJOINT characters (`*`, `_`, backtick), so no two matches can ever overlap — which is the argument that makes the two forms look interchangeable, and it is the wrong argument. The Elixir form RESCANS: a removal in pass 1 can bring two `_` together, and pass 2 then strips them. The Go form has already advanced past that position and never looks again.

MEASURED, 3 of 8 cases diverge — with 5 controls AGREEING, so the probe discriminates rather than reporting difference everywhere:

  "_**_"          go="__"        elixir=""
  "foo_**_bar"    go="foo__bar"  elixir="foobar"
  "a_**_b_**_c"   go="a__b__c"   elixir="abc"
  "*__*"          go="**"        elixir="**"       <- SAME
  "__**__"        go=""          elixir=""         <- SAME
  "_**bold**_"    both "_bold_"                    <- SAME
  "`a`"           both "a"                         <- SAME
  "**x**"         both "x"                         <- SAME

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE TELL, and it identifies the mechanism precisely: `_**_` diverges but its mirror image `*__*` does NOT, because the `**` pass runs FIRST. The bug is in pass ORDER plus rescanning, not in the patterns.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. These two are supposed to produce the SAME purpose-copy text from the same description — the CLI on create, the server on every subsequent write. Where they disagree, a row's mirror flips between two values depending on WHICH DOOR last wrote it, and a drift census then counts that row as drifted or not depending on which rule the census itself used.

IT HAS ALREADY POISONED A COUNT. gr-bl-brief-drift-backfill-714's criterion 2 says "normalises markdown exactly as the composer does" and cites the GO CLI — but the composer that decides the post-write state is the SERVER's. Its criterion 1 evidence already records a related contradiction: strict-composer normalisation gives 1,099 divergent, the baseline companion's method gives 1,007, against a published baseline of 714. WITH THIS FINDING THERE ARE THREE NORMALISATIONS IN PLAY, NOT TWO: the Go CLI's, the Elixir server's, and the baseline census's (markdown-strip PLUS control-byte strip PLUS whitespace collapse). Any figure quoted without naming which one produced it is unreproducible.

REACHABILITY, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The divergent shape needs `_` immediately followed by `**` immediately followed by `_` with nothing between — e.g. `foo_**_bar`. This is not common prose, and I have NOT measured how many live descriptions contain it. That measurement is criterion 3 below, and it decides whether this is a live defect or a latent one. Filing it as latent-until-measured is deliberate: the mechanism is proven, the blast radius is not.

MISS on the CROSS-LANGUAGE clause, honestly, and the reason is the fence - but the thing the clause actually needs now EXISTS. The criterion asks for a fixture BOTH suites read. PR #18714 ships it: internal/cli/testdata/brief_strip_corpus.json, 1,313 rows carrying input/one_pass/three_pass/family/divergent, and the Go half reads it (internal/cli/tasks_brief_strip_corpus_test.go). MEASURED AFRESH, and I am recording this as a MISS rather than a met on the lead's own standard: the naming clause is satisfied only once the tree carries the row, and that lands with PR #18714, not before. THE MEASUREMENT (2026-09-16, worker cli-r20-w54, independent of the earlier one): 9,786 task documents exported from production, 763 of them drafts; 9,769 carry a string description. Running the divergence predicate (one-pass output != three-pass output) over those 9,769: exactly ONE row diverges, task-8ba550b59141bccb - this row. CONTROLS PRINTED ON THE SAME RUN so the 1 cannot be read as a predicate that never fired: 1,177 descriptions contain **, 884 contain __, 3,948 contain a backtick, and the one-pass strip MODIFIED 4,582 of them. So the RULE is live on nearly half the corpus and the DIVERGENCE is latent in exactly one place. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, both to figures this lane published. (1) The denominator: PR #18522 quoted 9,356 live task descriptions; that is verbatim the 2026-09-10 count from tooling/grip/ledger/pds-tagregistry-twin-capture-2026-09-10.md and was not produced by that run. It is 9,769 as of 2026-09-16. (2) The '17 of them empty' is also mis-described: those 17 rows carry NO description key at all, not an empty string - there are ZERO empty-string descriptions. The VERDICT survives both corrections; the numbers did not. AN INSTRUMENT FAULT WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME: my first pass over the export read .content.description and found only 7 descriptions in 9,786 docs, which would have reported ZERO divergent rows. bp export FLATTENS content to the top level. Printing the key set - not reading the zero - is what caught it. PR #18714 names the row in internal/cli/tasks_brief_strip_corpus_test.go and tasks_brief_strip_parity_test.go, so a grep for 8ba550b59141bccb stops returning nothing; flip this criterion on that merge.
